title: SynGPU: Synergizing CUDA and Bit-Serial Tensor Cores for Vision Transformer Acceleration on GPU
problem: Vision Transformers suffer from quadratic time/memory complexity in self-attention, leading to inefficiency on GPUs despite token pruning methods overlooking bit-level sparsity.
motivation: Vision transformers are memory-bound; exploiting bit-level sparsity can improve compute efficiency beyond token-level sparsity.
method: Proposes Inter-token Bit-sparsity Awareness (IBA) algorithm exploring bit-sparsity from similar tokens. SynGPU enables GPU implementation via Bit-Serial Tensor Core (BSTC) supporting fixed- and floating-point MMA, with novel data mapping to enable full CUDA/Tensor Core parallelism.
key_novelty: Bit-Serial Tensor Core combining fixed-point BSDP and floating-point exponent alignment for efficient bit-sparse transformer compute.
contributions: Inter-token Bit-sparsity Awareness (IBA) algorithm exploiting bit-level sparsity across similar tokens
Bit-Serial Tensor Core (BSTC) supporting both fixed and floating-point operations
Novel data mapping enabling full parallelism of CUDA and Tensor Cores
2.15-3.95x speedup and 2.49-3.81x compute density improvement over A100
limitations: Applicability to other bit-width targets and transformer architectures beyond ViTs not discussed.
primary_theme: Bit-level sparsity exploitation for efficient vision transformer inference on GPU
